extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers who design/evaluate LLM math benchmarks (LLM benchmark curators, ML evaluation researchers, dataset authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, curating, and evaluating high-difficulty mathematics benchmark suites for large language models, with structure-aware item metadata, contamination controls, standardized grading, and diagnostics for model comparison across subjects and grade bands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure-first reasoning emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Items should target structure-first reasoning instead of heavy computation: emphasize logic/constraint puzzles, number-theoretic/combinatorial constructions, and spatial/geometry intuition over rote algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer problems that require identification and use of structural invariants (e.g., adjacency/constraint tables, cut/merge invariants) rather than long formula-chaining; design templates to foreground constructive witnesses and verifiable intermediate assertions. Anti-patterns: problems solvable by short memorized templates or pure numeric computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposable reasoning with verifiable intermediate assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Require decomposable reasoning steps and store minimal checkable invariants (process hooks) such that intermediate assertions can be validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For constraint puzzles provide canonical assignment tables; for spatial items provide vertex/edge transform logs; for number theory provide key lemmas (parity/modulo) as step-checkable artifacts to support process-aware verification and to detect 'correct-by-guess' cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce exposure bias via low-frequency patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize low-frequency surface patterns in candidate items to reduce contamination and prompt-overfitting to common classroom templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid high-frequency templates and templateable phrasing; use rule-based generation and rewrites to diversify surface forms while keeping solution structure. Anti-pattern: releasing many near-duplicate items with common templates that models likely memorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-source item construction pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Source items from a mix of human authoring, rule-based generation, and structure-preserving rewrites to diversify surface forms without changing solution structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed puzzle skeletons by humans, instantiate via rule generators (entity names, graph sizes), and apply structure-preserving rewrites and normalization for consistent style and answerability without diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-pass anti-contamination checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass every candidate through string-level n-gram fingerprinting, semantic-level embedding nearest-neighbor search, and template-level paraphrase detection to mitigate train–test leakage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite or remove high-similarity candidates; maintain per-item hash ids and publish an aggregate 'suspected overlap' statistic. Anti-patterns: skipping semantic-level checks or relying only on simple string matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item metadata and structural tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag each item with subjects (forced 7-way taxonomy), structural features (length, numeric-token density, symbolic-token count, constraint count, branching factor), and process hooks (required intermediate assertions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-label subject tags (Algebra, Calculus, Combinatorics, Geometry, Graph Theory, Number Theory, Probability). Record structural tokens and declarative process hooks to enable structure–performance analyses and process-aware scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified style and format normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite items for a uniform style (concise statements, explicit constraints) and format-normalize prompts to be answerable without diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent phrasing, indexing conventions, and explicitness of constraints to reduce misinterpretation. Normalize bilingual variants for parity across languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-checkable annotations (process hooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Store minimal checkable invariants per item that let graders verify step-level claims (e.g., uniqueness witnesses, invariants, monotonicity ranges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design verification hooks so future graders/verifiers can compute step validity and verifier agreement alongside final-answer checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control via solver/simulator validation and double annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply automated solver/simulator checks (CSP/SMT for logic uniqueness; simple simulators for spatial items) and double human annotation with arbitration for QC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solver checks to confirm uniqueness/consistency; use double annotation and arbitration to catch ambiguous phrasing or multiple valid interpretations. Anti-patterns: relying solely on human checks without solver validation for structured items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilingual normalization and parity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Bilingualize items (e.g., CN↔EN) and verify parity using back-translation and spot-checking of model agreement across languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure translated variants preserve difficulty and structural cues; use back-translation and model prediction consistency as parity signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty calibration through pilot runs and rank aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate item difficulty with a pilot of models and human raters; derive composite difficulty scores via rank aggregation over success rates and estimated step depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small-model pilots and human judgement to set difficulty bands and to stratify hardest-quintile (Q5) slices for diagnostic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frozen core plus controlled dynamic variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a frozen static core for comparability and provide controlled dynamic variants for future robustness stress tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a fixed evaluation split for longitudinal comparisons while allowing controlled, documented variants for stress-testing evaluation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert-driven curation and stage stratification (Contest track)
rubrics_metrics.description: Curate contest-style items by subject experts and stratify items across four stages (High School, Undergraduate, Graduate, Doctoral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix single-skill and cross-topic composite problems to reflect contest reality; deliberately include contest innovation items (multi-lemma reasoning, diagram-free geometry, constructive number theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven-subject forced taxonomy and multi-labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a forced seven-subject taxonomy (Algebra, Calculus, Combinatorics, Geometry, Graph Theory, Number Theory, Probability) with multi-label permitted to capture composite problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply full-credit multi-label analysis for subjectwise statistics (each item contributes fully to every tagged subject to avoid fractional bookkeeping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical answer forms and normalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Auto-grade to canonical final forms (integer, fraction, set, symbolic expression) with a normalizer for common radicals/fractions/ordering; apply numeric tolerance 1e-6 for floating outputs when floats are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize final answers via regex templates for integers, fractions, sets, and symbolic forms. Normalize units and equivalent formats. Anti-patterns: accepting inconsistent formatting or leaving normalization underspecified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary exact-match grading after normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply binary exact match (1/0) after normalization as the primary grading rule for released analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document that current public analyses focus on final-answer exact matches and that process-aware partial credit is out of scope for the initial release; future work will pair exact-match with process checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-label full-credit analysis convention
rubrics_metrics.description: When items carry multiple subject tags, analyses give full credit to each tagged subject rather than splitting credit fractionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simplifies per-subject aggregation and avoids fractional bookkeeping; note that this affects how subjectwise accuracies are interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation harness fairness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Query all models with the same harness, identical prompts, identical extraction rules, recording seeds and decode parameters; control rate limits and batching to reduce variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep decoding hyperparameters (temperature, top-p) identical within cost tiers; log seeds, parameters, and harness code for reproducibility. Anti-pattern: varying prompts or decoding settings across models without control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Chain-of-Thought prompting and small-sample self-consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to elicit stepwise reasoning and small-sample self-consistency to reduce output variance and improve reasoning performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine CoT with standardized extraction and identical decoding; record and report self-consistency sampling parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer extraction and regex-based normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize final-answer extraction using regex templates and normalizers for accepted output types (integers, fractions, sets, symbolic expressions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement regex rules and canonicalizers that map equivalent expressions (ordering, commutativity) to a canonical form before exact-match grading; document normalization rules publicly for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-aware scoring extensions (planned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complement exact-match grading with process-aware signals such as step validity, constraint fidelity, and verifier agreement computed from minimal per-item hooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stored invariants and process hooks to compute CoT-based scores indicating whether correctness arose from valid reasoning or from guesswork; plan to report aggregate process metrics alongside accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis metrics: hardest-quintile retention and structure–performance diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hardest-slice (Q5) retention, subject×model heatmaps, grade×model surfaces, radar profiles, and structure–performance relationships (e.g., sensitivity to numeric density, length, symbolic complexity) as discriminative diagnostics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Q5 retention (fraction retained from baseline) to reveal plan integrity under branching constraints; analyze numeric-density-driven error inflation, and examine weak/strong correlations between length/complexity and errors to identify dominant failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer-type and stage analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Disaggregate performance by answer type (numeric vs symbolic/derivational) and by grade stage (HS/UG/GR/PhD) to expose where symbolic/derivational forms or higher stages penalize accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how symbolic/derivational items impose percent-level penalties relative to numeric short answers and how stage scaling (HS→PhD) steepens leader–mid separations. Use these views to recommend targeted canonicalization or verifier efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect sensitive/licensed contest items (release policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release the reasoning diagnostic set (with metadata and graders) but withhold raw contest-style items that are sensitive/licensed, publishing only aggregate analyses and artifacts that reveal distributions without reconstructing items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance reproducibility with content sensitivity: provide figures, metadata distributions, and graders where possible but not item text when licensing or reuse risks contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-item provenance and overlap reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain per-item hash ids and release an aggregate 'suspected overlap' statistic to make anti-contamination checks auditable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log provenance metadata and make overlap statistics available so downstream users can assess contamination risk; update when items are rewritten or removed.
